modelIntro.title: What Is Kling 2.6 Motion Control?
description: Kling 2.6 Motion Control is a Kuaishou Kling video model for driving a character image with movement from a reference video. You provide the look to preserve and the motion clip to follow, then use the prompt to protect identity, outfit, framing, and style.

Use it for dance tests, portrait movement, fashion clips, presenter gestures, product-in-hand demos, and social videos where pose or body timing matters. On Toolaze, this flow uses one character image, one motion reference video, selectable Image or Video character orientation, and 720p or 1080p output.

metrics.label: Character image
metrics.value: 1 image, up to 10MB in the Toolaze uploader

metrics.label: Motion reference video
metrics.value: 1 MP4, QuickTime, or Matroska motion reference video, max 100MB, 3-30 seconds

metrics.label: Prompt
metrics.value: Optional; use it to preserve identity, outfit, framing, and style.

metrics.label: Duration
metrics.value: Image orientation supports 3-10 second references; Video orientation supports 3-30 seconds. Output duration follows the uploaded motion reference video.

metrics.label: Character orientation
metrics.value: Choose Image to match the character image orientation (3-10s reference) or Video to follow the reference video's character orientation (3-30s).

metrics.label: Motion control source
metrics.value: Pose, gesture, walk cycle, hand movement, and camera rhythm come from the uploaded video

metrics.label: Credit guidance
metrics.value: Credits scale with the uploaded motion reference video duration; current Toolaze rate is 22 credits per output second at 720p or 1080p.

metrics.label: Audio
metrics.value: Motion Control supports native audio on Toolaze, so generated clips can include sound alongside the controlled motion.

howToUse.title: How To Use Kling 2.6 Motion Control On Toolaze

steps.title: Choose Motion Control
steps.desc: Start with Kling 2.6 Motion Control selected so the generator expects both a character image and a motion reference video.

steps.title: Upload the character image
steps.desc: Use a clear image that shows the face, outfit, body shape, product, or visual style you want to preserve.

steps.title: Add the motion reference video
steps.desc: Upload one MP4, QuickTime, or Matroska clip (max 100MB, 3-30 seconds) with the pose, gesture, walk, dance, hand action, or camera rhythm you want to transfer.

steps.title: Set quality and refine
steps.desc: Choose 720p or 1080p; output duration follows the uploaded motion reference video. Generate, then simplify the prompt or use a cleaner motion clip if identity, limbs, or framing drift.

faq.q: What is Kling 2.6 Motion Control on Toolaze?
faq.a: It is an image-to-video generator flow for applying motion from one reference video to one uploaded character image while preserving identity, outfit, and visual style.

faq.q: Can I create from a prompt only?
faq.a: No. Kling 2.6 Motion Control requires both a character image and a motion reference video. Choose another Toolaze video model if you do not have motion footage.

faq.q: Is the prompt required for Motion Control?
faq.a: No. The character image and motion reference video are required; the prompt is optional and useful for preserving identity, outfit, lighting, framing, and style.

faq.q: Can I upload a driving video for motion transfer?
faq.a: Yes. Upload one motion reference video together with one character image. The video supplies pose, gesture, timing, camera rhythm, and the final output duration.

faq.q: How many reference files can I use?
faq.a: Toolaze supports one character image and one motion reference video for this flow. The uploader accepts motion videos in MP4, QuickTime, or Matroska, up to 100MB and 3-30 seconds.
Kling 2.6 Motion Control on Toolaze supports 720p and 1080p output options.
Yes. Toolaze enables native audio for Kling 2.6 Motion Control, so generated clips can include sound together with the transferred motion.

faq.q: How many credits does it use?
faq.a: Credits scale with the uploaded reference-video duration. The current Toolaze rate is 22 credits per output second for 720p or 1080p Motion Control.

faq.q: Is Kling 2.6 Motion Control free to use?
faq.a: Video generation uses Toolaze credits. Starter credits, available settings, reference-video length, and final cost can vary by account quota and resolution.

faq.q: How do I write a stronger prompt?
faq.a: Keep the prompt short and protective: preserve identity, outfit, lighting, framing, and style while following the uploaded motion reference. Remove extra scene changes that compete with the video.

faq.q: Should I choose Motion Control or Kling 3.0?
faq.a: Choose Motion Control when you have a motion reference video and need a character image to follow it. Choose Kling 3.0 when you want broader prompting, more image references, 4K, or longer scene planning.
